events.what: Heinrich, Kiyomi, Otachi and Schweitzer prove interval graphs with at least three vertices are reconstructible (polynomial-time)
O'Shea and Wilkins claim a full proof of the reconstruction conjecture (Information Sciences 654, 119858)
events.credibility_reason: Pre-snapshot; not taken up by specialists, later sources (ProofAtlas, Wikipedia) still call the conjecture open. Covers undirected graphs only, not the digraph conjecture, so at most a case of the bullet. Primary text not opened.

events.what: DeepMind AlphaEvolve-based agent formulates and proves a bipartite variant of graph reconstruction
events.ai_basis: produced a complete proof for one of those variants

judgement.doubts: The bullet bundles two conjectures; even a full undirected proof would be only a case. The DeepMind bipartite result uses a different deck/equivalence notion and self-chosen hypotheses, so variant; if its exact statement turns out to be a strict subclass case, it would join the partial tier and ai_role could rise under Step 4. O'Shea-Wilkins is pre-snapshot and cannot set status regardless.

corrections.why: F8: the AI work (arXiv 2605.22763) concerns bipartite variants with altered deck/isomorphism notions per the record's competing_reading; status rests on the human interval-graphs preprint, so none. Would change only if the bipartite theorem proves to be a strict case.
